why: The statement asks only whether the pair (p, p+6) recurs infinitely often. Bounded-gap results (Zhang, Maynard, Polymath8b, and the 2026 240/236/212/186/182 wave) bound H1, the smallest recurring gap, which is a different question: H1 at most 186 says nothing about gap 6 specifically, and even the conditional H1 at most 6 allows gaps 2 or 4 to carry the recurrence. So they are variants, not bounds on this problem. Mor-Gupta (positive proportion of admissible tuples) likewise does not reach {0,6}. Holt and Caicedo-Ramos state no theorem for p+6 and score none; the Axiom 246 formalisation is a formalisation of known results. The only events claiming the whole question (Lynch, Zhang-Zhang-Zhang Polignac, Tan) carry several F10 signals together: self-publication or a general-math dump, claims to defeat the parity barrier by elementary or numerical means, version churn or self-contradictory 'unconditional' framing, and no uptake on a landmark problem, so they are not_credible. AI roles: the 186 and 182 events are generated by their own attributions; the Axiom 212 event names AxiomProver only for verification, so none.
doubts: The 186 and 182 AI attributions rest on a tracker rendering and a faculty listing line; primary PDFs were unread. Credit to these AI events is moot for this problem since they are variants. The Zhang-Zhang-Zhang first-upload date (v1-v10) is unknown but plainly after the snapshot.
